51435082.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to BRD4 bromodomain 1 (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by ITC assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Panalytical) at 25 °C. The CREBBP bromodomain (100 μM) or BRD4(1) bromodomain (100 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the ligand (100 μM) was loaded into the syringe. The buffer used was 20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 0.01% Tween-20, pH 7.5. The stirring speed was set to 750 rpm. The ligand was injected in 20 μL aliquots, with 180 s between injections. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal) with a one-site binding model. The experiments were performed in triplicate, and the data are presented as the mean ± standard deviation. The binding affinity (Kd) was calculated from the binding isotherm. The thermograms and binding isotherms are shown in Figures S11 and S12.

51435101.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human BRD4 bromodomain 1 assessed as dissociation constant by ITC assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Panalytical) at 25 °C. The protein (CREBBP or BRD4(1) bromodomain) was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, pH 7.5, and concentrated to 100 μM. The ligand was dissolved in DMSO and diluted in the same buffer to a final concentration of 1–2 mM. The protein was loaded into the sample cell (200 μL), and the ligand was loaded into the syringe (200 μL). The titration consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a 120 s spacing between injections. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (MicroCal) with a one-site binding model. The heats of dilution were determined by titrating the ligand into buffer and subtracted from the raw data. The dissociation constant (Kd) was calculated from the binding isotherm. The experiments were performed in triplicate, and the data are presented as the mean ± standard deviation.
